# Javahiru'l-Asrar (Gems of Divine Mysteries)
## BH00012

*Translated on 17 Qudrat 183 using GPT 6.1 Sol*

**1** Gems of mysteries in the ascending stages of journeys, for whoever desires to draw near to God, the All-Powerful, the Ever-Forgiving. Blessed are the righteous who drink from these rivers.

**2** He is the Exalted, the Most High.

**3** O you who travel the paths of justice and gaze upon the countenance of grace! Your letter has arrived, I have understood your question, and I have heard the melodies of your heart within the pavilion of your inmost being. I have therefore raised the clouds of the will to shower upon you the rains of wisdom, that they may take from you all you have acquired before, turn you from the realms of opposition toward the sanctuary of oneness, and bring you to the shore of holiness, so that you may drink from it, your soul may find rest there, your thirst may subside, your heart may be refreshed, and you may be among those who are guided today by the light of God.

**4** Although in these days, when the dogs of the earth and the beasts of the lands have surrounded Me, I have concealed Myself in My secret retreat and am prevented from revealing the wonders of His knowledge, the gems of His wisdom, and the manifestations of His power that God has bestowed upon Me, nevertheless I do not wish to disappoint one who has stood before the sanctuary of grandeur, desires to enter the pavilion of eternity, and longs to soar in the heaven of this new beginning at the dawn of decree. I will therefore recount to you something of what God has graciously bestowed upon Me, within what souls can bear and minds can sustain, lest the clamor of the malicious and the banners of the hypocrites be raised. I ask God to assist Me in this, for He is the most merciful of the merciful and the Giver to those who ask.

**5** Know that you should first consider why the various peoples now on earth did not believe in the Messengers of God, whom God sent through His power, raised up to establish His Cause, and made the lamp of His eternity within the niche of His oneness. Why did they turn away from them, disagree about them, oppose them, contend with them, and wage war against them? For what reason did they acknowledge neither their mission nor their authority, but instead denounced them as unbelievers and reviled them, even killing and banishing them?

**6** O you who walk in the wilderness of knowledge and dwell in the ark of wisdom! Unless you understand the mystery of what We have recounted to you, you will not attain the degrees of faith or be assured of the Cause of God, the Manifestations of His Cause, the Dawning-Places of His wisdom, the Treasuries of His revelation, and the Mines of His knowledge. You will be among those who have not striven in the Cause of God, have not caught the fragrance of faith from the garments of certitude, have not attained the ascending heights of unity, and have not reached the stages of singleness within the embodiments of praise and the essences of detachment.

**7** Strive, then, My brother, to understand this station, so that the veil may be lifted from the face of your heart and you may be among those whose sight God has made keen, that you may behold the primal realities of the realm of might, discover the mysteries of the kingdom and the symbols of the divine Essence in the lands of humanity, and attain the station in which you see no disparity in the creation of the All-Merciful and no flaw in the creation of the heavens and the earth.

**8** Now that the discussion has reached this most lofty and difficult station and this most radiant yet formidable mystery, know that these peoples, the Jews and the Christians, denied the Cause of God, turned away from His Messengers, and rejected His proofs because they did not understand the purport of the words or attain what God had promised them in His Book. Had they looked at the proof itself and not followed every ignorant rabble-rouser among their scholars and leaders, they would have reached the treasury of guidance and the sanctuary of piety, and drunk of the living, life-giving water in the city of the All-Merciful, the garden of the All-Glorious, and the reality of paradise. But because they did not behold the proof with their own eyes, which God had created for them through those Messengers, and desired something other than what God, through His grace, desired for them, they became far removed from the pavilion of nearness, were barred from the river of reunion and the wellspring of grace, and lay dead within the veils of their own selves.

**9** Now, through the power and strength of God, I will recount some of what God mentioned in the books of old, and the signs of the revelations of oneness in the embodiments of detachment, so that you may recognize the station of daybreak in this eternal morning, behold this fire blazing in a tree neither of the East nor of the West, open your eyes upon attaining your Lord, and let your heart partake of the blessings concealed in these hidden vessels. Thus may you thank God, your Lord, for singling you out for this and making you one of those who are certain of meeting their Lord.

**10** This is the text of what was revealed before in the Gospel of Matthew, in the first book, where He mentions the signs of the appearance of the One who will come after Him and says: “Woe to pregnant women and nursing mothers in those days,” until the Dove sings at the center of eternity and the Cockerel of the Throne raises its call in the farthest tree, the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary, and says: “Immediately after the distress of those days, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light, the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of heaven will be shaken. Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming upon the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. And He will send His angels with the sound of the mighty trumpet.” Here ends the quotation.

**11** In the second book, in the Gospel of Mark, where the Dove of holiness speaks, it says: “In those days there will be distress such as has not occurred from the beginning of what God created until now, and never will.” Here ends the quotation. After this, it sings as it sang before, without change or alteration. God is the witness to what I say.

**12** In the third book, in the Gospel of Luke, He says: “There will be signs in the sun, the moon, and the stars, and on earth distress among the nations at the terror of the sea’s roar and the earthquakes, and the powers of heaven will be shaken. And they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds with power and great glory. When you see all this taking place, know that the kingdom of God has drawn near.” Here ends the quotation.

**13** In the fourth book, in the Gospel of John, He says: “When the Comforter comes, whom I will send to you, the Spirit of Truth who comes from the Truth, He will testify about Me, and you too will testify.” In another passage He says: “When the Holy Spirit, the Comforter whom My Lord will send in My name, comes, He will teach you everything and remind you of everything I have told you. Now I am going to the One who sent Me, and none of you asks Me, ‘Where are You going?’ because I have told you this.” In another passage He says: “I tell you the truth: it is better for you that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Comforter will not come to you. But if I go, I will surely send Him to you. When that Spirit of Truth comes, He will guide you into all truth, for He will not speak on His own authority, but will speak what He hears and tell you what is to come.”

**14** This is the text of what was revealed before, and, by God, besides whom there is no other god, I have indeed been brief. Were I to recount the words of the Prophets among what was revealed to them from the dominion of grandeur and the kingdom of sovereignty, pages and tablets would be filled before I reached their end. In all the scriptures, psalms, and sacred writings there is to be found and mentioned the like of what I have recounted and imparted to you—indeed, what is loftier and greater than everything I have mentioned and explained. Were I to wish to recount all that was revealed before, I could indeed do so through the wonders of His knowledge and power that God has bestowed upon Me. But I have contented Myself with what I have explained to you, lest you grow weary on your journey and turn back on your heels, and lest sorrow, gloom, hardship, humiliation, or exhaustion overtake you.

**15** Be fair, then, and reflect on these exalted utterances. Then ask those who claim knowledge without any clear evidence from God or any proof from Him, and who have remained heedless of these days in which the sun of knowledge and wisdom has risen from the horizon of divinity and gives everyone their due and everyone of rank their proper measure and station: what do they say about these allusions, which minds are bewildered to comprehend and holy souls are perplexed to fathom, with the consummate wisdom of God and the knowledge of God concealed within them?

**16** If they say that these words are from God, admit of no interpretation, and are to be taken according to the outward wording in its most literal sense, how can they object to these unbelievers among the people of the Book? For when those people saw in their Book what We have recounted to you, and their learned men explained it to them according to the outward wording, they therefore did not acknowledge God in the Manifestations of oneness, the Dawning-places of singleness, and the Temples of detachment. They neither believed in them nor obeyed them, because they had not seen the sun darkened, the stars falling from heaven onto the face of the earth, or the angels descending to earth in outward bodily form. Thus they opposed the Prophets and Messengers. Indeed, when they found them at variance with their religion and their laws, they assailed them with charges of falsehood, madness, unbelief, and error that I am ashamed to recount to you. Look again in the Qurʾan, and you will find all this and understand it. From that day to this, this people have awaited the appearance of what they have learned from their learned men and accepted with certainty from their jurists, saying, “When these signs appear, we will surely believe.” If the matter were so, how could you refute their argument, invalidate their proof, and contend with them concerning their religion, what they have learned from their books, and what they have heard from their leaders?

**17** And if they say that these scriptures, which this people possess, which they call the Gospel and attribute to Jesus son of Mary, did not descend from God and the Manifestations of His own Self, it follows that the flow of grace from its all-bountiful Source was interrupted, that God's proof to His servants was not conclusive, that His blessing was not complete, His providence not radiant, and His mercy not all-embracing. For if Jesus was raised to heaven and His Book was taken up, by what could God establish His case against them on the Day of Resurrection and punish them, as the leaders of religion have written and rightly guided scholars have expressly stated?

**18** Reflect within yourself, then: when you see the matter to be so, as We also see it, where will you flee, to whom will you hasten, and toward whom will you turn? In what land will you dwell, on what resting place will you sit, and on what path will you stand firm? At what hour will you sleep, by what means will you bring your affair to its conclusion, and with what will you secure the handle of your religion and the cord of your obedience? No, by Him who has revealed Himself in oneness and to whose singleness you bear witness! If a spark of the fire of God's love were to arise in your heart, you would neither sleep nor remain still, neither laugh nor rest. Rather, you would flee to the mountain peaks in the court of nearness, holiness, and beauty. You would lament as the bereaved lament and weep as those who yearn weep, and you would not return to your home and dwelling until God disclosed His Cause to you.

**19** As for you, who ascend to the dominion of guidance and rise to the kingdom of piety: if you wish to understand these sacred allusions, behold the mysteries of knowledge, and become acquainted with the all-embracing Word, you must ask about all this, and about everything that comes before you concerning your origin and your return, of those whom God has made the wellspring of His knowledge, the heaven of His wisdom, and the ark of His mystery. For without these lights shining from the horizon of the divine Essence, people cannot tell their right from their left. How, then, could they ascend to the horizon of realities or reach the treasury of subtleties? We therefore ask God to admit us into these surging seas, to honor us with access to these outpouring spirits, and to establish us on these divine ascents, so that we may strip from our persons everything we have acquired from our own selves and remove from our bodies all the borrowed garments we have stolen from others like ourselves, that God may clothe us in the robes of His providence and the garments of His guidance.

**20** And may He admit us into the City of Knowledge, where whoever enters will know all sciences before turning toward its mysteries, and will learn all knowledge and wisdom concerning the mysteries of lordship deposited in the treasuries of creation from the leaves that have sprouted from its trees. Exalted is God, who brought it into being and originated it, above all He has created within it and ordained for it! By God, the All-Protecting, the All-Powerful, the Self-Subsisting! If I were to show you the gates of this City, which was created by the right hand of power and might, you would see what no one before you has seen, behold what no soul other than you has beheld, and understand the obscure meanings of its indications and the perplexing subtleties of its allusions. The mysteries of the beginning would be demonstrated to you in the point of the end, all things would become easy for you, fire would be made light, knowledge, and mercy for you, and you would be among those at rest upon the expanse of holiness.

**21** Without this, and without all the gems of the mysteries of wisdom We have imparted to you in the depths of these blessed, spiritual words, you cannot comprehend even a drop from the vast oceans of knowledge and the deep rivers of glory. By the finger of the divine Essence, through the Pen of Oneness, you would be inscribed as ignorant in the Mother Book, and neither a single letter of the Book nor the words of the family of God concerning the mysteries of the beginning and the return would be unraveled for you.

**22** Be fair, then, you servant whom We have not seen outwardly, but whose love We have found inwardly. Place yourself in the presence of Him who sees you even if you do not see Him, and who knows you even if you do not know Him. Can anyone explain those words with sound evidence, clear proofs, and manifest allusions to such a degree that the questioner's heart finds rest and the one addressed is reassured? No, by Him in whose hand is My soul! No one can drink even a drop from them except one who enters the shade of this City, whose foundations are built upon mountains of crimson ruby, whose wall is of the chrysolite of oneness, whose gates are of the diamond of eternal self-sufficiency, and whose dust is of the fragrance of generosity.

**23** Now that We have mentioned and imparted to you some of the mysteries, though veiled and concealed, We return to Our earlier discussion of what We have learned from the books of the past, so that your foot may not slip in anything and you may be certain of all that We have sprinkled upon you from the surging oceans of life in the divine realm of names and attributes.

**24** It is written in all the books of the Gospel as follows, when the Spirit spoke with light and said to His disciples, “Know, then, that the heavens and the earth may pass away, but My words will never pass away.” You are aware that the meaning of these words, according to their outward expression, can only be that these books of the Gospel will remain among the servants forever, that their ordinances will not expire nor their proof perish, and that everything He prescribed in them, defined for them, and ordained through them will endure and never pass away.

**25** Therefore, My brother, purify your heart, illumine your inmost being, and sharpen your sight, so that you may recognize the melodies of the birds of the divine Essence and the songs of the doves of holiness in the kingdom of everlasting life, and understand the interpretation of the words and their mysteries. Otherwise, if you interpret them according to their outward expression, you will never be able to establish the Cause of Him who came after Jesus, nor will you be able to confute your opponent and prevail over the obstinate among these people who associate partners with God. For the scholars of the Gospel invoke this verse as evidence that the Gospel can never be abrogated: “Even if those signs written in our books should appear and the promised Person should be manifested, He must judge among the servants according to the ordinances of the Gospel. Even if all the signs written in the books should appear, if He rules otherwise than Jesus ruled, we will neither acknowledge nor follow Him.” This is one of the tenets they accept as certain, just like what you witness today in the objections raised by the learned and the ignorant among the people.

**26** They say, “The sun has not risen in the west, the crier has not cried out between heaven and earth, certain lands have not been submerged, the Dajjal has not appeared, the Sufyani has not arisen, and the Figure has not appeared in the sun.” With My own ears I heard one of their learned men say, “Even if all those signs should appear and the awaited Qaʾim should be manifested, if He rules otherwise than what was revealed in the Qurʾan concerning the subsidiary laws we possess, we will surely denounce Him as a liar and kill Him, and will never acknowledge Him.” Such things these deniers say, even after the Resurrection has come to pass, the trumpet has been sounded, all who are in the heavens and the earth have been gathered, the Balance has been set up, the Path has been laid down, the verses have descended, the sun has shone forth, the stars have been blotted out, souls have been raised, the spirit has been breathed forth, the angels have been arrayed, Paradise has been brought near, and the fire has been kindled. All this has been accomplished, yet to this very moment none of them has understood, as though they were dead beneath their veils, except those who have believed and returned to God, who today rejoice in the Paradise of holiness and walk in God's good pleasure.

**27** Because all people were veiled by the coverings of their own selves, they did not recognize the melodies of holiness, did not inhale the fragrances of grace, and did not inquire of the people of remembrance, even though God had commanded them to do so. He said—and His word is true—“Ask the people of remembrance if you do not know.” Instead, they turned away from the people of remembrance and followed the Samiri according to their own desires. Thus they became far removed from God's mercy and failed to attain His beauty on the day of meeting Him, even though all had awaited the day of His appearance and had prayed to God by night and day to gather them into His presence, so that they might suffer martyrdom in His path, be guided by His guidance, and be illumined by His light. Yet when He came to them with a sign from God and a proof from His presence, they declared Him an unbeliever, reviled Him, and did to Him what they did, to such a degree that neither can I recount it nor can you bear to hear it. At this the Pen cries out, and the ink weeps and screams. If you were to listen with the hearing of your innate nature, by God, you would hear the lamentation of the inhabitants of the heavens. If you were to lift the veil from your eyes, you would see that the maidens of heaven have fainted and the spirits have fallen senseless, striking their faces and sitting upon the dust.

**28** Alas, alas for what befell the Manifestation of God's own Self, and for what they did to Him and His loved ones—such things as no one has done to another, no soul to another soul, no unbeliever to a believer, and no believer to an unbeliever. Alas, alas! The Temple of eternity has sat upon the black dust, the Holy Spirit has lamented in the retreats of the Most Exalted, the pillars of the Throne have collapsed in the most resplendent realm of divinity, the life of existence has been transformed in the crimson land, and the tongue of the Dove has fallen silent in the golden dominion. Shame on them, on what their hands have earned, and on all that they have done!

**29** Listen, then, to what the Dove has sung concerning them in the most beautiful, wondrous melodies and the most perfect, exalted warblings, that it may be a cause of remorse to them from that day until the day when people stand before the Lord of the worlds: “Previously they had prayed for victory over those who disbelieved, but when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So God's curse is upon the liars.” Such is their condition and the extent of their attainment in this vain life. They will be returned to the torment of the blazing fire, and they will find for themselves neither protector nor helper.

**30** Do not let all that was revealed in the Qurʾan, or what you have heard from the writings of the Suns of infallibility and the Moons of grandeur concerning the distortions of the extremists and the alterations of those who pervert the text, become a veil for you. By those words they intended only certain specific, expressly designated instances. Despite My helplessness and poverty, if I wished to set forth for you what is mentioned, I could do so. But then the intended aim would elude Us, We would stray from this outstretched path, become submerged in allusions to what is limited, and depart from what is beloved in the court of the All-Praised.

**31** And you, who are mentioned in this outspread parchment and illumined amid this pitch-black darkness by the lights of the Mount that have shone upon you on the Sinai of revelation, purify yourself of all the evil allusions and idolatrous indications you have previously known, so that you may inhale the fragrance of eternity from the Joseph of faithfulness, enter the Egypt of the cloud of unknowing, and perceive the sweet fragrances of splendor from this radiant, snow-white Tablet, through the mysteries of eternity that the Pen has inscribed within it concerning the names of its Lord, the Exalted, the Most High, that you may be recorded among those who possess certitude in the Tablets of holiness.

**32** Then know, you who are present before this Servant while unaware of it, that whoever wishes to undertake the journeys through the ascending paths of the mysteries must strive in religion to the full extent of his strength and ability, so that the way may become manifest to him along the paths of proof. If he finds a person who lays claim to a Cause from God and holds in his hand a proof from his Lord that the peoples of the world are powerless to match, he has no recourse but to follow him in everything he commands, says, and decrees—even if he applies to water the law of earth, or to earth the law of heaven, or what is above or below that, and even if he decrees change or alteration. For he is acquainted with the mysteries of the divine Essence, the symbols of the unseen, and the divine ordinances.

**33** If all the servants among the various nations were to act according to what We have mentioned, their task would then become easy for them, and those expressions and allusions would not prevent them from entering the depths of the names and attributes. Had they understood this, they would not have denied God's blessings, fought against the Prophets, repudiated them, or rejected them. You will find expressions like these in the Qurʾan, if you reflect upon it.

**34** Then know that through words such as these God tests His servants, sifts them, and distinguishes the believer from the unbeliever, the detached from the attached, the doer of good from the wrongdoer, the devout from the wretched, and others like them. Thus has the Dove of the divine Essence proclaimed: “Alif Lam Mim. Do people suppose that they will be left to say, ‘We believe,’ without being put to the test?”

**35** The traveler toward God, who leaves his home in His path, must detach himself from everyone in the heavens and on earth and restrain himself from everything other than Him, so that the doors of providence may be opened before his face and the breezes of loving-kindness may blow upon him. When he has made binding upon himself the gems of meaning and utterance that We have imparted, he will recognize all the allusions in those indications, and God will send down upon his heart a tranquility from His presence and make him one of those who dwell in peace. Through such revealed words of ambiguous meaning, then, understand what you have asked of this Servant, who sits at the lowest point of abasement and walks the earth only as a stranger who finds for himself neither helper, companion, loved one, nor supporter. He places His trust in God and says at every moment, “We belong to God, and to Him we return.”

**36** Our description of these words as ambiguous applies only to those who have not ascended to the horizon of guidance or attained the degrees of recognition in the retreats of providence. But for those who have recognized the stations of the Cause and witnessed the mysteries of divine guardianship in what God has imparted to their souls, all the verses are clear and all the allusions firmly established. They recognize the mysteries deposited within the garments of words just as you recognize heat from the sun and moisture from water—indeed, more clearly than that. Exalted is God above what We have said in speaking of His loved ones! Exalted is He above what they recount!

**37** Now that We have reached this most resplendent station and attained this sweetest summit through what flows from this Pen by the supreme providence of God, the Exalted, the Most High, We wish to mention to you some of the stations of the servant's progress in his journeys toward his Origin, so that all you have desired and now desire may be disclosed to you, that the proof may be conclusive and the blessing complete.

**38** Know, then, and recognize that at the outset of his journey toward God the wayfarer must enter the garden of search (Search: the first city of holiness on the path of the glory of seeking). On this journey the wayfarer should detach himself from everything other than God and close his eyes to everyone in the heavens and on earth. His heart must harbor neither hatred for any servant nor love for anyone to a degree that would prevent him from reaching the retreat of Beauty. He must sanctify himself from the veils of glory. It is incumbent upon him not to exalt himself over anyone on account of anything God has given him, whether the adornments of this world, outward learning, or anything else. He must seek the Truth with the utmost earnestness and endeavor, so that God may teach him the ways of His providence and the paths of His bounty, for He is the best helper of His servants and the finest supporter of His bondsmen. He said—and His word is true—“Those who strive for Us, We will surely guide to Our ways,” and elsewhere, “Be mindful of God; God will teach you.”

**39** On this journey the wayfarer witnesses alterations and changes, differences and correspondences. He beholds the wonders of lordship within the mysteries of creation and becomes acquainted with the ways of guidance and the divine paths. This is the station of the seekers and the ascending paths of those who pursue their goal.

**40** When he ascends beyond that station, he enters the city of love and attraction (Love: the surging of a fiery sea in the city of love’s attraction). Then the winds of love blow and spiritual breezes stir. In this station, transports of longing and breaths of spiritual delight seize the wayfarer, so that he no longer knows right from left, land from sea, or deserts from mountains. At every moment he burns with the fire of yearning and is set ablaze throughout the horizons by the overpowering force of separation. He races through the Paran of love and the Horeb of attraction. At times he laughs, at times he weeps; at times he is still, at times he is restless. He cares for nothing; no matter restrains him and no decree bars his way. He awaits his Lord’s command at his beginning and his end, expends his spirit at every moment, and sacrifices himself at every instant. He offers his breast to the spears of his enemies and raises his head to the sword of destiny. Indeed, he kisses the hands of whoever kills him and gives up everything that is his and everything incumbent upon him, that he may sacrifice his spirit, his self, and his body in the path of his Lord—but with his Beloved’s permission, not from his own desire. You find him cool in fire and dry in water. He dwells in every land and walks every road. Whoever touches him in that state will feel the heat of love coming from him. He walks upon the lofty plane of detachment and races through the valley of inaccessibility. His eyes remain ever expectant of the wonders of God’s mercy and the sight of the lights of His beauty. Blessed are those who attain! This is the station of the lovers and the condition of those drawn to Him.

**41** When he completes this journey and ascends beyond this most great station, he enters the city of unity (Unity: the radiance of wonders of sanctity in the city of the glory of oneness), the garden of singleness, and the court of detachment. In this station the wayfarer casts aside all allusions, indications, veils, and expressions, and beholds things with the very eye through which God has revealed Himself to him. On this journey he witnesses how all differences return to a single word and all allusions end in a single point, as attested by the saying of the one who boarded the ark of fire and walked at the pivot of journeys until he reached the loftiest summit in the dominion of everlasting life: “Knowledge is a point that the ignorant have multiplied.” This is the station mentioned in the tradition: “I am He and He is I, except that He is He and I am I.”

**42** In that station, if the embodiment of the Seal were to say, “I am the Point of the beginning,” he would speak the truth; and if he were to say, “I am other than it,” that too would be true. If he were to say, “I am the Lord of the earthly and heavenly kingdoms,” or “the King of kings,” or “the Sovereign of the dominion of might,” or “Muḥammad,” or “ʿAlī,” or “their descendants,” or anything else, he would be speaking truth from God and exercising authority over all contingent beings and everything besides Him. Have you not heard what was handed down before: “Our first is Muḥammad, our last is Muḥammad, and our middle is Muḥammad,” and elsewhere, “They are all of one light”?

**43** In that station the truth of unity and the signs of detachment are established. You find that all of them have raised their heads from the bosom of God’s power and enter the sleeves of God’s mercy, without your perceiving any distinction between the sleeves and the bosom. To conceive of change or alteration in this station is sheer association of partners with God and pure unbelief, for this is the station of the revelation of oneness, the expression of singleness, and the shining of the lights of the dawn of eternity in the lofty mirrors that receive their imprint. By God, if I were to describe this station to the extent God has ordained for it, spirits would be severed from their bodies, essences would descend from their places, everyone in the depths of contingent existence would be struck senseless, and everything moving in the lands of allusion would cease to exist.

**44** Have you not heard, “There is no alteration in God’s creation”? Have you not read, “You will find no alteration in His way”? Have you not witnessed, “You see no disparity in the creation of the All-Merciful”? Indeed, by my Lord, whoever belongs to this ocean’s depths and has boarded this ship witnesses no alteration in God’s creation and sees no disparity in God’s earth. Since there is no alteration or change in God’s creation, how could it affect the Manifestations of God’s own Self? Glorified, then, is God beyond what We have said in describing the Manifestations of His Cause, and exalted is He above what they recount.

**45** God is most great! This sea has laid up its stores, and the wind has stirred a wave that casts forth pearls. Strip off your garments and drown in it; abandon swimming, for the swimmer has nothing to boast of.

**46** If you belong to this city within these depths of oneness, you will see all the Prophets and Messengers as one temple, one self, one light, and one spirit, so that their first is their last and their last is their first. All arose for the Cause of God, ordained the laws of God’s wisdom, and were the Manifestations of God’s Self, the mines of God’s power, the treasuries of God’s revelation, the dawning places of God’s sun, and the daysprings of God’s light. Through them the signs of detachment appeared in the realities of contingent beings, the tokens of singleness in the essences of existing things, the elements of glorification in the essential realities of oneness, and the seats of praise in the pure realities of eternal self-sufficiency. Through them He originates creation, and to them He returns all things that can be mentioned. Just as in their inner realities they are one in light and one in mystery, so behold them in their outward appearances, that you may recognize them all as one temple—indeed, find them to be one utterance, one discourse, and one exposition.

**47** In that station, if you were to call their first by the name of their last, or the reverse, it would be true, as the decree concerning this has descended from the Source of Divinity and the Wellspring of Lordship: “Say: Call upon God or call upon the All-Merciful; whichever you call upon, His are the most beautiful names.” For they are the manifestations of God’s name, the daysprings of His attributes, the seats of His power, and the focal points of His sovereignty. He, exalted and mighty, is in His essence sanctified above all names and transcends the ascending heights of attributes. Behold, then, the traces of God’s power in the horizons of their spirits and in their very temples, that your heart may be assured and you may be among those who journey through the horizons of nearness.

**48** I will now renew My discourse to you on this station, that it may assist you in recognizing your Creator. Know that God, blessed and exalted, will never appear in His own being or His own essence. He has always remained concealed in the eternity of His essence and hidden in the everlastingness of His being. When He wished to reveal His beauty in the dominion of names and display His majesty in the kingdom of attributes, the Prophets appeared from the unseen into the visible world, that His name the Manifest might be distinguished from His name the Hidden, and His name the First might become apparent apart from His name the Last, so that the saying might be fulfilled: “He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He encompasses all things.” He placed the manifestations of those greatest names and these most exalted words within the Manifestations of His Self and the mirrors of His being.

**49** It is thus established that all names and attributes refer to these sanctified, transcendent Lights. You find all names in their names and all attributes in their attributes. In that station, if you were to call them by every name, it would be true, just as their existence is true. Recognize, then, what is intended in this exposition, and conceal it within the pavilion of your heart, that you may understand the matter about which you asked and attain it to the extent God has ordained for you. Perhaps you may be among those who attain what God intends.

**50** Everything you have heard concerning Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan—may the spirit of everyone in the depths of the world of spirits be sacrificed for him—is true beyond doubt, and we all believe in it. Yet the Imams of the Faith stated that he was in the city of Jābulqā, and they described this city as having strange features and wondrous signs. If you wish to explain this city according to the outward meaning of the tradition, you will be unable to do so and will never find it. For even if you search the regions of the world and the farthest reaches of its lands, you will not find it with the characteristics they described before, even if you travel the earth for as long as God’s eternity and the permanence of His sovereignty endure. The whole earth could neither contain nor support it. If you show Me the way to this city, I will show you the way to this holy Soul, whom people have known according to what they themselves possess, not according to what he possesses. Since you cannot do that, you must interpret these traditions and reports handed down from these Lights. Just as you need interpretation for the tradition related concerning this city, so too you need an interpretation concerning this preexistent Soul. Once you understand this interpretation, you will have no need for alteration or anything else.

**51** Know, then, that since the Prophets are all one spirit, one soul, one name, and one designation, you will, with this eye, see that all the Manifestations bear the name Muḥammad, that their fathers are named Ḥasan, that they have appeared from the Jābulqā of God’s power, and that they appear from the Jābulṣā of God’s mercy. Jābulqā is none other than the treasuries of everlasting life in the dominion of the cloud of unknowing and the cities of the unseen in the divine realm on high. We testify that Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan was in Jābulqā and appeared from it, and that He whom God will make manifest is within it until God manifests Him in the station of His sovereignty. This we acknowledge, and in them all we believe. We have been brief concerning the meanings of Jābulqā in this passage, but you will recognize all these meanings in the mysteries of these Tablets, if you are among those who are certain.

**52** But concerning Him who appeared in the year sixty, you have no need of either alteration or interpretation, for His name was Muḥammad and He was a descendant of the Imams of the Faith. Thus it is true of Him that He is the son of Ḥasan. This is known to you and evident to your presence. Indeed, He is the creator of the name and its originator for Himself, if you look with the eye of God.

**53** At this point We wish to leave what We have been discussing and recount what befell the Point of the Qur’an, becoming one of those who tell of it, so that you may gain insight into all matters from One who is mighty and beautiful.

**54** Know, then, and reflect on His days, when God raised Him up for His Cause and manifested Him in the station of His own Self: how the people attacked Him, opposed Him, and disputed with Him. Whenever He walked before them in the streets and markets, they mocked Him, shook their heads at Him, and ridiculed Him. At every moment they sought to kill Him, until the earth, for all its vastness, became narrow for Him. The inhabitants of the Concourse on high were bewildered at His plight, the pillars of everlasting life gave way to extinction, and the eyes of the people of the cloud of unknowing wept over Him. These wicked unbelievers inflicted on Him what those who are faithful cannot bear to hear.

**55** Had these evildoers reflected on their own condition, recognized the melodies of that Dove upon the boughs of this snow-white Tree, been content with what God had sent down to them among His blessings, and found the fruits of the Tree upon its branches, they would not have opposed and denied Him, after they had all stretched their necks in longing to reach Him and had asked God at every moment that His beauty might honor them and that He might grant them the bounty of meeting Him.

**56** Indeed, because they did not recognize the melody of oneness, the mysteries of the divine Essence, or the intimations of holiness in what issued from the tongue of Aḥmad, and did not reflect within themselves, but followed the false divines who turned God’s servants away in former cycles and will turn people away in cycles to come, they were veiled from God’s purpose. They did not drink from the river of the divine Essence and were deprived of meeting God, the Manifestation of His being and the Dayspring of His eternity. Thus they walked the paths of error and the ways of heedlessness and returned to their abode in the fire whose fuel was their own selves. They were recorded as unbelievers by the Pen of God in the Book of Holiness, and they found no friend or helper for themselves, nor will they find one until that time.

**57** Had these people held fast to the very Handle of God in the garment of Muḥammad, turned to God with their whole being, and cast aside everything they had received from their divines, God would have guided them by His grace and made known to them the holy meanings within His eternal words. For God is too exalted and too great to turn a petitioner away from His door, disappoint one who hopes at His threshold, drive away one who seeks refuge in His shade, deprive one who clings to the hem of His mercy, or banish a poor soul who has alighted at the watering place of His wealth. But because these people did not turn to God with their whole being or cling to the hem of His mercy spread abroad through the appearance of the Sun of oneness, they left the shade of guidance and entered the city of error. Thus they became corrupt and corrupted His servants, went astray and led astray everyone in the lands, and were inscribed among the wrongdoers in the books of heaven.

**58** Now that this fleeting servant has reached this lofty station in explaining the allusions to these meanings, I will tell you, with the utmost brevity, the reason for the opposition of these hardhearted people, so that it may be a guide for those of understanding among those endowed with insight, and a gift from this servant to all believers.

**59** Know that when the Point of the Qur’an and the Light of the All-Glorious came with decisive verses and radiant proofs, verses that everyone in the dominion of existence is powerless to produce, He commanded all to stand firm upon this exalted path, stretched forth in everything He had brought from God. Whoever acknowledged Him and recognized the signs of oneness in His heart and the beauty of eternity in His beauty, He declared to have attained resurrection, ingathering, life, and paradise. For after believing in God and the Manifestation of His beauty, such a person was raised from the grave of heedlessness, gathered into the land of His heart, quickened with the life of faith and certitude, and admitted to the paradise of His presence. Is there any paradise higher than this, any ingathering greater than this, or any resurrection more momentous than this resurrection? Were anyone to discover its mysteries, he would know what no one among the peoples of the world has known.

**60** Know, moreover, that this paradise in the Day of God is greater than all paradises and more sublime than the realities of Riḍwān. For God, blessed and exalted is He, after sealing the station of prophethood in His Beloved, His chosen One, the One He selected from among His creation—as was sent down from the kingdom of glory, “But He is the Messenger of God and the Seal of the Prophets”—promised His servants that they would meet Him on the Day of Resurrection, because of the greatness of the subsequent Revelation, as has indeed come to pass. There is no paradise greater than this and no rank higher than this, if you reflect on the verses of the Qur’an. Blessed, then, is the one who is certain of meeting Him on the day His beauty is revealed.

**61** Were I to recount for you the verses sent down concerning this lofty rank, the discourse would grow long and you would be drawn away from the purpose. But I will mention this verse, and We will content Ourselves with it, so that your eyes may be gladdened and you may attain what is treasured and stored within it. It is this: “God is He who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see, then established Himself upon the throne and subjected the sun and the moon, each running its course for an appointed term. He directs all affairs and sets out the signs, so that you may be certain of meeting your Lord.”

**62** Consider, then, My beloved, the mention of certitude in this verse. It is as though the heavens, the earth, the throne, the sun, and the moon were all created so that His servants might be certain of meeting Him in His days. By God, My brother! Look at the greatness of this station and the condition of these servants in these days: they are like startled asses fleeing from the divine Countenance and the beauty of the divine Essence. If you reflect on what We have sent down to you, you will discover Our purpose in this utterance and recognize what We have desired to teach you in this garden, so that your eyes may be gladdened by gazing upon it, your hearing delighted by listening to what is recited within it, your soul enriched by comprehending it, your heart illumined by recognizing it, and your spirit rejoiced by the fragrance wafting from it; that you may attain the utmost outpouring of God’s grace and be among those who dwell forever in the garden of holiness.

**63** But whoever turned away from God in His person, withdrew and rebelled, then disbelieved and fell into misery, He pronounced upon him the judgment of idolatry, unbelief, death, and fire. What idolatry is greater than turning to the manifestations of Satan and following the divines of forgetfulness and the companions of rebellion? What unbelief is greater than turning away from God on the day when faith is renewed by God, the All-Powerful, the All-Bountiful? What death is more abject than fleeing from the Source of the Ever-Living, the One who is Life itself? What fire is hotter than remoteness from the beauty of the divine Essence and the majesty of oneness on the day of loss and beneficence?

**64** The Arabs of the age of ignorance objected to Him on account of these expressions and words, passed the judgments against Him that they did, and said, “These people who have believed in Muḥammad were with us and associated with us every night and day. When did they die, and on what day did they return?” Listen, then, to what was sent down concerning what they said: “If you marvel, marvelous indeed is their saying, ‘When we have become dust and bones, will we truly be raised up?’” And in another passage: “If you say, ‘You will surely be raised up after death,’ those who disbelieve will say, ‘This is nothing but manifest sorcery.’” Thus they mocked and ridiculed Him, for they had seen the words “death” and “life” in their books and heard them from their divines, and had interpreted them as outward death and bodily life. When they did not find what they had understood through their groundless suppositions and their lying, malicious minds, they raised the standards of discord and the banners of corruption and kindled the fire of war, even though God extinguished it through His power, just as you witness today from these idolaters and these evildoers.

**65** Now that the fragrance of rapture has wafted over Me from the city of eternity, and the surging forces of longing have surrounded Me from the direction of the dawning light, as the Sun of the horizons has shone from the region of Iraq and caused Me to hear the melodies of the Hijaz concerning the mysteries of separation, I wish to mention to you something of what the Dove has sung at the heart of the cloud of unknowing concerning the meaning of life and death. Yet this is impossible, for if I wished to explain it to you as it is written in the Preserved Tablets, spirits could not bear it, pages could not contain it, and souls could not endure it. Nevertheless, I will speak as befits this time and this hour, that it may be a guide for anyone who wishes to enter the pavilion of meanings, hear spiritual melodies from this divine, spiritual Bird, and be among those who have detached themselves from all but God and rejoice today in meeting Him.

**66** Know that life has two stations. One concerns the outward human condition in the elemental body. This is as well known to you and to everyone on earth as the sun in the middle of the sky. This life ends with outward death. This is a truth from God, and no one can escape it. But the life mentioned in the books of the Prophets and the holy ones is nothing other than the life of spiritual recognition: the servant’s recognition of the sign of the revelation of the One who reveals Himself to him, through that by which He has revealed Himself to him in His own person, and his certainty of meeting God in the Manifestations of His Cause. This is the good, abiding, everlasting life. Whoever lives through it will never die, but will abide through the abiding of his Lord and endure through the endurance of his Creator.

**67** The first life, which is connected with the elemental body, comes to an end, in accordance with what has been sent down from God: “Every soul will taste death.” But the second life, which comes from spiritual knowledge, does not come to an end, as was sent down before: “We will surely grant him a good life,” and, in another passage concerning the martyrs: “Rather, they are alive, sustained in the presence of their Lord.” It is also related in the traditions: “The believer is alive in both worlds.” Many such words are found in the books of God and the Manifestations of His justice. For brevity, We have not wished to mention them, and have contented Ourselves with this for what We intended for you.

**68** Then, My brother, turn away from your desires and turn toward your Master. Do not follow those who have made their desires their god, so that you may enter the heart of life beneath the shelter of salvation granted by the Nurturer of names and attributes. For those who have turned away from their Lord today are dead, even though they walk the earth; deaf, even though they hear; and blind, even though they see. The Master of the Day of Judgment has explicitly declared this: “They have hearts with which they do not understand, and eyes with which they do not see,” and so on to the end of the passage. Indeed, they walk along the edge of a crumbling bank, or on the brink of a pit of fire. They have no share of this surging, overflowing ocean, and amuse themselves with the embellishments of their own words.

**69** Now, in this connection, We convey to you what was sent down before concerning life, so that it may turn you away from the promptings of the self, free you from the confines of the cage amid these coursing, receding stars, and make you one of those who are guided through the darkness of the earth.

**70** He said—and His word is the truth—“Is someone who was dead, whom We brought to life and for whom We made a light by which he walks among people, like someone who is in darkness and cannot emerge from it?” This verse was sent down concerning Ḥamza and Abū Jahl, when the former believed and the latter disbelieved. Most of the divines of the age of ignorance mocked at this, became confused, made jests, and cried out, saying, “How did Ḥamza die, and how did he return to his former life?” There is much like this in the Book, if you examine the verses of God discerningly.

**71** If only I could find pure hearts, that I might cast upon them a sprinkling from the oceans of the knowledge My Lord has taught Me, so that they might fly through the air as they walk upon the earth, run upon water as they run upon the dust, take their souls in their hands, and sacrifice them in the path of their Creator. But permission has not been given to pronounce upon this supreme mystery. This secret has always been stored in the treasuries of power, and this mystery concealed in the repositories of might, lest the servants destroy themselves in the hope of attaining this most great station in the realms of eternity. Those who walk in the darkness of blackest night will never attain it.

**72** My brother, We have repeated Our words at every point so that, by God’s permission, everything set down in these lines may become clear to you, that you may have no need of those who plunge into the depths of darkness and walk in the valley of pride and delusion, and that you may be among those who journey in the paradise of the Ever-Living, the One who is Life itself.

**73** Say: People of the assembly of \[conjecture\]! The Tree of Life has been planted in the midst of God’s paradise and bestows life in every direction. How is it that you neither perceive nor recognize it? The song of the Dove of Holiness in the paradise of eternity confirms for you all the jewels of the mysteries of the divine Essence that We have conveyed to you from this assured Soul. I will recount it to you so that you may put on a new garment made of blocks of iron, to protect you against the doubts hurled at those allusions. It is this: “Whoever is not born of water and the Spirit cannot enter the Kingdom of God, for what is born of the flesh is flesh, and what is born of the Spirit is spirit. So do not marvel at My saying that you must be born again.”

**74** Then fly to the divine Tree, take of its fruits, gather what has fallen from it, and be its faithful guardian. Reflect on what one of the Prophets said when he gave souls the glad tidings of the One who would come after him through veiled allusions and concealed symbols, rather than speaking openly, so that you may be certain that none but those endowed with understanding recognize their words. He went on to say: “His eyes were like a flame of fire, His feet were like brass, and from His mouth came a two-edged sword.” How, then, are these words to be interpreted? If someone were to appear with these signs in their outward sense, he would not be a human being, and how could anyone feel at ease with him? Indeed, when he appeared in one city, you, the people of another city, would flee from him, and no one would ever approach him. Yet if you reflect on these expressions, you will find them supremely eloquent and consummately expressive, having ascended to the summit of utterance and reached the utmost station of exposition. It is as though the suns of eloquence have appeared from them and the stars of lucid speech have risen and shone from them.

**75** Then recognize these foolish ones among the peoples of the past, and those who in these days await the coming of that Man. Unless this Soul comes in the form described, they will never believe in Him; and since He will never come in this way, they will never believe. Such is the extent of the understanding of these unbelieving, idolatrous souls. How can those who do not recognize the most self-evident of truths and the most manifest of things recognize the subtleties of the divine principles and the jewels of the mysteries of the wisdom of the Eternal?

**76** I will now briefly explain these words to you, so that you may recognize the mysteries and be among those who understand them. Learn, then, and judge fairly what We convey to you, so that in this arena you may be remembered before God as one of the fair-minded.

**77** Know that the one who spoke these words in the arenas of glory intended to describe the attributes of the One who would come through concealed meanings and riddles, so that those attached to outward appearances would not discover Him. As for his saying, “His eyes were like a flame of fire,” he meant only the keenness of the sight of the One who would come and the power of His insight, such that with His eyes He burns away every veil and covering. Through them He recognizes the mysteries of eternity in the worlds of earthly dominion and distinguishes those whose faces are overspread with the gloom of hell from those in whose faces you recognize the radiance of bliss. If His eyes were not of God’s kindled fire, how could He burn away the veils and everything that is in people’s hands, behold the signs of God in the dominion of names and the kingdom of things, and witness all things through the all-seeing eye of God? Thus have We made His sight keen today, if you are certain of the signs of God. What fire is hotter than this fire that has shone upon the Sinai of His eyes, through which He has burned away everything by which the servants have veiled themselves in the lands of existence? Glory be to God for the mysteries of the beginning and the return that have appeared in the Tablets of rectitude, until the day when the caller proclaims: “Then, indeed, we are all returning to God.”

**78** As for his saying, “His feet were like brass,” he meant only steadfastness when He hears the call of God: “Stand firm, as you have been commanded,” so that He may remain steadfast in the Cause of God and abide on the path of God’s power. Even if everyone in the heavens and on earth were to deny Him, His feet would not falter in proclaiming the message, nor would He flee from what God has commanded Him to ordain. His feet would be like towering mountains and lofty peaks. He would be firm in obedience to God and unwavering in manifesting His Cause and setting forth His Word. No one’s obstruction would turn Him back, no opponent’s prohibition would deter Him, and no unbeliever’s denial would cause Him regret. Whatever denial, hatred, unbelief, and wickedness He witnesses, His love for God increases, the longing in His heart grows, the ardor in His inmost being intensifies, and love declares itself within His breast. Have you seen on earth brass firmer than this, iron stronger than this, or a mountain more immovable than this? For He stands on His feet against everyone on earth and fears no one, despite what you know of people’s deeds. Glory be to God, who gives Him repose and raises Him up! He indeed has power over whatever He wills, and He is the All-Protecting, the Self-Subsisting.

**79** “And from His mouth came a two-edged sword.” Know that, since the sword is an instrument of cutting and separation, and from the mouths of the Prophets and the holy ones comes what separates the believer from the unbeliever and severs the lover from the beloved, it was given this name. By this he meant only cutting and separation. For example, when the Primal Point and the eternal Sun wishes to gather together all creatures by God’s leave, raise them from the resting places of their own selves, and separate them from one another, He utters a verse from God. This verse separates truth from falsehood from that day until the Day of Resurrection. What sword is sharper than this sword of oneness, and what blade keener than this blade of eternal self-sufficiency, which severs every tie? Through it He separates those who turn toward Him from those who turn away, father from son, brother from sister, and lover from beloved. For whoever believes in what has been sent down to Him is a believer, and whoever turns away is an unbeliever. The separation between this believer and this unbeliever becomes such that they will never associate or come together in the world. So too with father and son: if the son believes and the father denies, they are separated and will never be of one kind. Indeed, you see the son killing the father, and the reverse. In this way, understand everything We have mentioned, explained, and set forth in detail.

**80** If you were to behold with the eye of certainty, you would see that this divine sword divides even the loins, if only you knew. This proceeds from the word of separation that appears on the day of separation and sundering, if only people would take heed in the days of their Lord. Indeed, if you sharpened your sight and softened your heart, you would see that all the outward swords that slay unbelievers and wage war against the wicked in every age and time proceed from this inward, divine sword. Open your eyes, then, to discover everything We have shown you and attain what no one among all peoples has attained. And We say: “Praise be to God, for He is the Master of the Day of Judgment.”

**81** Because these servants did not draw knowledge from its source and proper place, or from the sweet, fresh, palatable sea that flows by God’s leave within pure and unalloyed hearts, they were veiled from God’s intention in His words and allusions, and remained dwelling in the prison of their own selves.

**82** We thank God for what He has bestowed upon Us through His grace, and for making Us certain of His Cause, before which the heavens and the earth cannot stand, acknowledging Him on the day of meeting Him and acknowledging Him whom God will make manifest in the next Resurrection. He has made Us among those certain of Him before His manifestation, so that His favor to Us and to all the worlds may be complete.

**83** But I complain to you, My brother, of those who claim affiliation with God and the Manifestations of His knowledge, yet commit indecencies, devour people’s wealth, drink wine, take lives, steal property from one another, backbite one another, invent falsehoods about God, and lie in most of what they say. People attribute all this to Us. They feel no shame before God, abandon what God has commanded them, and commit what they have been forbidden, whereas the people of truth should show signs of humility in their faces and the lights of holiness in their countenances. They should walk the earth like one walking in God’s presence and be distinguished from everyone on earth in every movement and moment of stillness, so that with their eyes they witness the signs of His power, with their tongues and hearts they remember God, with their feet they walk toward the homelands of nearness, and with their hands they take hold of God’s ordinances. Were they to pass through a valley of gold and mines of silver, they would pay them no heed and would not turn toward them.

**84** Yet these people have turned away from all this and turned toward whatever their desires crave. They wander in the valley of pride and delusion. I testify, therefore, that God is clear of them, and We are clear of them. We ask God not to bring Us together with them, either in this world or in the next. He indeed is the Truth; there is no god but Him, and He has power over all things.

**85** Drink, then, My brother, of this water that We have caused to flow in the seas of these words. It is as though the oceans of grandeur surge within them and the jewels of oneness shine for them, through them, and upon them. Strip off the garments of whatever prevents you from entering this deep crimson sea. Say, “In the name of God and through God,” then enter it. Fear no one, and place your trust in God, your Lord. “Whoever places his trust in God, He is sufficient for him.” He will indeed protect you, and within it you will be among those who are safe.

**86** Know, moreover, that in this most subtle and most glorious city you will find the wayfarer humble before every face and reverent before all things, for he beholds nothing without seeing God within it, and witnesses His light in all that the lights of revelation have encompassed upon the Sinai of contingent existence. In this station he must not occupy the seats of honor in gatherings to glorify himself, nor take precedence over anyone out of self-importance. He must see himself at every moment in his Lord’s presence, not approve for anyone what he would not approve for himself, not say to anyone what he could not bear to hear from another, and not wish for anyone what he would not wish for himself. He must move upon the earth along the line of rectitude in the kingdom of unfolding decree.

**87** But know that, at the beginning of his journey, the wayfarer indeed sees transformation and change, as We mentioned before. This is a truth beyond doubt, as was revealed in describing those days: “The day when the earth is changed into another earth.” This is one of those days whose like no eyes have witnessed. Blessed is the one who attains them and recognizes their worth. “We indeed sent Moses with Our signs: ‘Bring the people out of darkness into light, and remind them of the days of God.’” This is one of the days of God, if only you knew.

**88** In this station, all changing and transformed things are present before you. Whoever affirms otherwise has strayed in the Cause of God, disputed His sovereignty, and waged war against His rule. He who changes the earth and makes it another earth is indeed able to change everything upon it and everything moving across its surface. Do not be astonished at this, for He has changed darkness into light and light into darkness, ignorance into knowledge, error into guidance, death into life, and life into death. In this station the rule of transformation is established, if you are among those who follow this path. Reflect upon it, so that what you have sought from this lowly One may appear to you from the pavilion of this proof, and you may be among those dwelling within it. For He does whatever He wills and ordains whatever He desires. He is not questioned about what He does, while all are questioned about everything.

**89** But, My brother, in this degree—that is, at the beginning of the journey, as We mentioned in the city of search—you will see different stations and varying signs. All are true in their proper places and stations. In this station you should behold all things in their proper places, without bringing anything down from its elevation and loftiness or raising anything from its station and lowliness. For example, if you were to make divinity dwell within humanity, this would be sheer association of partners with God; and if you were to raise humanity into the atmosphere of divinity, this would be pure unbelief. But if you speak of divinity in divinity and humanity in humanity, this is a truth beyond doubt. That is, if you were to behold transformation in the worlds of divine unity, this would be a sin greater than any in existence. But if you behold transformation in its proper station and understand it as you should, no blame rests upon you.

**90** By My Lord, despite all We have imparted to you of the mysteries of expression and the stations of explanation made manifest, it is as though I had not mentioned a single letter from the ocean of God’s hidden knowledge and the essence of His treasured wisdom. We shall speak of these in their time, if God so wills and desires. He indeed makes mention of everything in its proper station, and We all make mention of Him.

**91** Know, then, that the bird that flies in the atmosphere of dominion cannot fly in the heaven of the holiness of divinity, nor can it mingle the fruits God has created there or drink from the rivers that flow there. Were it to drink a drop from them, it would die at once, as you witness in these days among those who ascribe themselves to Us, yet do what they do, say what they say, and claim what they claim. It is as though they were dead within their veils.

**92** Understand all the stations, allusions, and indications in this way, and you will recognize everything in its proper place and find every matter in its proper station. To this station—that is, the station of the city of oneness—belong men who have embarked upon the ark of guidance and journeyed along the ascending paths of oneness. \[You behold the lights of beauty shining from their faces and the mysteries of majesty from their persons.\] You perceive the fragrance of musk in their words and observe the signs of sovereignty in their gait, their movements, and their stillness. Do not let yourself be veiled by the deeds of those who have not drunk from the pure springs or reached the cities of holiness, who follow their own desires, spread corruption on earth, and imagine themselves rightly guided. They are those of whom it has been said: “A mindless rabble, followers of every clamorous voice, swaying with every wind.” The degrees of this journey, this station, and this homeland are known to you and evident to your eyes; there is no need to dwell on them at length.

**93** Know, then, that whenever you have seen or heard that the Sun of Truth and the Primal Point ascribed to Himself any of the names of the past, this was solely because of the weakness of His servants and the ordering of the worlds of creation. Otherwise, all names and attributes circle around His Essence and revolve within the precincts of His sanctuary. Indeed, He is the nurturer of names, the manifestation of attributes, the giver of essence to all essences, the revealer of signs, and the embellisher of tokens. Were you to behold with your inner eye, you would find all besides Him absent in His presence and nonexistent in His court. “God was, and nothing was with Him,” and now He is as He has ever been. Since it is established that He—glorified and exalted be He—was, and nothing was with Him, how can the law of alteration and change apply? Reflect, then, upon what We have imparted to you, so that the sun of guidance may appear to you in this eternal dawn and you may be among those who are detached within it.

**94** Know, then, that all We have said in describing these journeys was intended only for the learned among the righteous. Were you to mount the steed of the spirit and travel through the divine gardens, you would traverse all these journeys and discover the mysteries before your eyes could turn back to you.

**95** Then, My brother, if you are a horseman of this arena, gallop through the realms of certitude, so that you may free yourself from the prison of associating partners with God in this day and catch the scent of musk from the breezes of this garden. From the perfume of this city, fragrant breezes have spread throughout the regions of the world. Do not deprive yourself of your share, and do not be among the heedless.

**96** How well he said: “If the breaths of her fragrance spread in the East, someone in the West whose nose was blocked would regain his sense of smell.”

**97** After this divine journey and this spiritual ascent, the wayfarer enters the garden of bewilderment (the bewilderment of a holy spirit’s ascent in the valley of the light of bewilderment). This is a station which, if it were disclosed to you, would make you weep and lament for this Servant, who remains in the hands of these associators of partners with God, bewildered in His plight and among those lost in wonder in this ocean. Every day they consult about killing Me, and every hour they seek My expulsion from this city, just as they expelled Me from other lands. I, this Servant, stand before them, awaiting what God has decreed for Us, ruled concerning Us, and ordained for Our souls. I fear no one and am wary of no soul, although hardship and affliction have encompassed Us at the hands of the people of oppression and hatred, and sorrows have enveloped Us in these times. “Beside My lamentation, Noah’s flood is but as My tears, and the kindling of the fires of Abraham but as My burning anguish. Jacob did not pour forth even the least of My sorrow, and all the afflictions of Job are but a portion of My tribulation.”

**98** Were I to recount to you the afflictions that have descended and the events that have befallen Us, you would grieve so deeply that all remembrance would cease for you, and you would become oblivious to your own existence and to everything God has created in His dominion. Since We did not desire this for you, I have concealed the disclosure of this decree within the heart of Bahāʾ and veiled it from all that moves in the land of creation, so that it may remain hidden within the pavilion of the unseen until God reveals its mystery. For nothing in the heavens or on earth escapes His knowledge, and He is watchful over all things.

**99** Since We have strayed from the intended subject, We leave these allusions and return to Our account of this city: whoever enters it is saved, and whoever turns away from it perishes.

**100** Know, you who are mentioned in these Tablets, that whoever embarks upon this journey becomes bewildered by the evidences of God’s power and the wondrous signs of His handiwork. Bewilderment seizes him from every direction and on every side, as the Essence of Eternity testified in the Concourse on High with His words: “My Lord, increase my bewilderment in You.” And how well it has been said:

**101** “I was not bewildered until I chose love for You as my way. How bewildered I would be if my bewilderment were not in You!”

**102** In that valley you wayfarers lose your way and perish, and you cannot reach their abode. God is greater than the grandeur of this valley and the vastness of this city in the dominion of creation! It is as though you could find neither its beginning nor its end. Glad tidings, then, glad tidings to the one whose journey within it is complete, whom God has aided to traverse this goodly land in this divine city, where all who are brought near and all who are sincere are bewildered. And We say: “Praise be to God, the Lord of the worlds.”

**103** Should the servant ascend and journey away from this earthly homeland, desiring to ascend to the divine homeland, he will enter from this city into the city of annihilation (the annihilation of the singing of \[divine\] effacement in the garden of the swoon of annihilation), through his annihilation of self and his abiding in God. In this station, this pure and most exalted homeland, this journey of supreme effacement, the wayfarer forgets his self, his spirit, his body, and his being. He swims in the ocean of annihilation and is on earth as one who was not a thing worthy of mention. No one will perceive in him any traces of existence, for he has vanished from the realms of the visible and attained the stations of effacement.

**104** Were We to recount the mysteries of this city, the realms of the heart would perish from their inhabitants’ intense longing for this station of rectitude. For this is the station where the Beloved reveals Himself to the true lover, and where the radiance of the Loved One’s lights appears to the lover who is free of all attachment.

**105** Can the lover have any existence when the Beloved reveals Himself, or the shadow remain when the sun appears, or the lover endure in the presence of the Loved One? No, by Him in whose hand is My soul! Indeed, were the wayfarer in this station to search the east and west of the earth, its land and sea, its plains and mountains, he would find neither himself nor anyone else, so complete is his annihilation in the One who brought him into being, and so subtle his effacement in his Creator.

**106** Glory be to God! Were it not for My fear of the Nimrod of oppression and My protection of the Abraham of justice, I would impart to you what would make you independent of all besides yourself, and recite to you what would bring you near this city when you are oblivious to your self and your desires. But be patient until God brings forth His command. He indeed rewards the patient without measure. Breathe, then, the spiritual fragrance from the garments of inner meanings, and say: “People of the ocean of annihilation, hasten to enter the city of abiding, if you would ascend the ascending paths of abiding.” And We say: “We belong to God, and to Him we return.”

**107** From that most exalted, most exalted station and that greatest, most resplendent rank, he enters the city of abiding (the abiding of the singing of an everlasting dove in the valley of the holiness of abiding), to abide there. In that station the wayfarer beholds himself upon the throne of independence and the seat of exaltation. Then the import of what was said before becomes apparent to him: “The day when God enriches everyone out of His abundance.” Blessed is the one who has reached this station and drunk from this white cup in this crimson sanctuary.

**108** For when the wayfarer on this journey becomes immersed in the oceans of abiding, empties his heart of all else, and reaches the ascending heights of life, he never sees annihilation for himself or for anyone else. He drinks from the cup of abiding, walks in the land of abiding, flies in the air of abiding, sits with the embodiments of abiding, and partakes of enduring, everlasting bounty from the everlasting, eternal tree. He is numbered among the people of abiding, remembered through abiding in the heights of abiding.

**109** Everything in this city is enduring and everlasting, never passing away. Were you, by God’s permission, to enter this lofty and exalted garden, you would find its sun at the zenith, never eclipsed and never setting. So too are its moon, its heavens, its stars, its trees, its seas, and everything within it and belonging to it. By God, besides whom there is no other god, were I to recount to you the wondrous attributes of this city from this day until the end that has no end, My heart’s love for this good and everlasting city would not be exhausted. But I bring these words to a close because time is short and the seeker is pressing, and so that the mysteries may not be openly disclosed without permission from God, the All-Powerful, the All-Subduing.

**110** In the resurrection to come, those who affirm God’s unity will behold Him whom God will make manifest descending with this city from the heaven of the unseen, accompanied by the angels who are exalted and brought near. Blessed is the one who enters His presence and attains reunion with Him. We all hope for this, and We say: “Praise be to God, for He is the Truth, and to Him we shall all return.”

**111** Know, then, that if anyone who reaches these stations and travels on these journeys is touched by pride or conceit along the way, he will perish at once and return to the first step without realizing it. The sign of those who have arrived and those who yearn on these journeys is that they lower their wings before those who believe in God and His verses, humble themselves before those who have drawn near to God and the Manifestations of His beauty, and bow before those established upon the lofty seat of God’s Cause and grandeur.

**112** For even if they ascend to the furthest limit in their journey toward God and their attainment of Him, they will reach only the dwelling created within their own hearts. How, then, could they ascend to stations that have not been ordained for them or created for their condition? Even if they journey from eternity to eternity, they will never reach the Pole of existence and the Center of being, to whose right flow the seas of grandeur and to whose left flow the rivers of power. No one can alight in His courtyard, much less attain His station. He dwells in the ark of fire, sails upon the sea of fire within the sphere of fire, and walks in the air of fire. How, then, can one created of opposites enter the fire or draw near it? If he approaches it, he will burn at once.

**113** Know, then, that if this most great Pole were to sever the thread of His sustaining grace from all who are in the heavens and on earth, they would all cease to exist. Glory be to God! How can dust reach the Lord of lords? God is far above what they imagine within themselves, and exalted beyond what they say.

**114** Indeed, the wayfarer ascends to a station without limit within what has been ordained for him, and finds in his heart the fire of love, so intense that it wrests the reins of choice from these righteous souls. At every moment he grows in love for his Lord and in his turning toward his Creator, to such a degree that, were his Lord in the east of nearness and he in the west of remoteness, and were he to possess red pearls and yellow gold enough to fill the heavens and the earth, he would spend it all and hasten on his very eyes to reach the land where the Desired One dwells. If you find the wayfarer otherwise, know that he is a lying impostor. We belong to Him whom God will make manifest in the resurrection to come, and through Him we shall be raised.

**115** In these days, since We have not lifted the veil from the face of the Cause or \[shown\] the servants the fruits of these stations, which We have been prevented from revealing, you find them drunk with heedlessness. Otherwise, were less than a needle’s eye of this station disclosed to everyone on earth, you would see how they would gather in the courtyard of God’s mercy and hasten from every direction to reach the precinct of nearness upon the lofty seat of God’s might. But We have concealed it for the reasons We mentioned before, and so that the believers may be distinguished from the deniers, and those who turn toward Him from those who turn away. And I say: “There is no strength or power except through God, the All-Protecting, the Self-Subsisting.”

**116** From this station the wayfarer ascends to the city (the unseen ascent of eternal holiness in the countenance of a hidden mystery), which has no name, no trace, no mention, and no sound. Within it flow the seas of eternity, and they circle around eternity. Within it the sun of the unseen shines from the horizon of the unseen. It has heavens of its own and moons of its own light, all rising from the sea of the unseen and entering the sea of the unseen. I cannot mention even a sprinkling of what has been ordained within it. No one knows its mysteries except God and the Manifestations of His own Self, for He is its Creator and Originator.

**117** Know, then, that when We wished to address these words and had written some of them, We intended to explain to you everything We had previously mentioned of the words of the Prophets and the utterances of the Messengers, in the melodies of those brought near and upon the heights of the sanctified. But We found no opportunity and were granted no respite by this traveler who came from you, for he was hasty in the matter and hurried in his decision. We have therefore been brief and contented Ourselves with this, and have not completed the account of all the journeys as would be fitting and appropriate. Rather, We have left unmentioned the greater cities and the mightier journeys. The bearer’s haste reached such a point that We left unmentioned the two most exalted journeys, those of surrender and contentment.

**118** Yet, were you to reflect on these brief words, you would come to know all knowledge, attain the summit of the Known, and say: “This suffices for all existence, both what is seen and what is absent.”

**119** But if you find within yourself the heat of love, you will say: “Is there more?” And We say: “Praise be to God, the Lord of all worlds.”
